title: Echo Chamber described as absent-character reactions
skill_evidence: references/agents.md:113 "`echo-chamber` (Echo Chamber — Misc) — absent characters / sidebar reactions to the current scene"; :32 "Echo messages (absent characters reacting to the current scene)"
reality: Echo Chamber simulates a live, streaming-style fictional audience reacting to the roleplay, shown in a floating Echo widget that reveals one queued reaction at a time (30 s by default), with named audience-style prompt options (AO3 / Wattpad, Twitter / Reddit, 4chan, Constructive, Hype Squad, Harbingers) and widget controls Re-run Echo Chamber / Clear messages; Parallel, Roleplay. Sources: docs/agents/built-in-agents.md 'Echo Chamber'; docs/agents/agents-overview.md ('A live audience reaction agent runs here'); en.json ui.chat.chatsettingsdrawer.promptModeControlsTheFictionalAudienceStyleUsedFor = 'Prompt mode controls the fictional audience style used for live roleplay reactions.'; stable catalog v3 description 'Simulates a live streaming-style chat reacting to your roleplay in real time.' Nothing in docs or code describes absent characters.
fix: agents.md:113 → 'live fictional-audience reactions to the Roleplay scene in a floating Echo widget, revealed one at a time; pick the audience style (AO3 / Wattpad, Twitter / Reddit, 4chan, Constructive, Hype Squad, Harbingers) as its Prompt Mode'. Keep the v2.1 fresh-messages-only note. agents.md:32 → 'Live audience reactions (Echo Chamber)'.

title: Historical-accuracy example uses nonexistent {{message}} macro and a fictional rewrite wiring
skill_evidence: references/agents.md:457 promptTemplate ends 'The passage:\n{{message}}'; :458 '"settings": {}' (no resultType); :462 'and (if wired to a rewrite agent — `continuity` or `prose-guardian`) trigger rewrites on issues'
reality: macro-engine.ts has no `message` macro (the switch handles `input` etc.; unknown macros are left as-is, macro-engine.ts:3104 'leave unknown macros as-is'), so the literal text '{{message}}' reaches the model. Post-processing agents already receive the finished reply automatically (agent-executor.ts:2864-2866 formatAgentMainResponseForPrompt). docs/prompts/macros.md lists `{{input}}` and no `{{message}}`. Nothing lets a custom agent's output trigger Prose Guardian or Continuity Checker: post-processing Turn Data Access exposes only Pre-generation injections and Parallel agent results (docs/agents/custom-agents.md 'Pipeline Phase'). With no resultType, the agent is a Context Injection that only records a note after generation.
fix: Example: delete 'The passage:\n{{message}}' (say 'You will receive the latest reply'). Then either make it a Text Rewrite agent (resultType text_rewrite + capability edit_messages, returning editedText/changes) to fix anachronisms in place, or keep context_injection and say its note reaches the next turn through Add as Prompt Section / {{agent::historical_accuracy_regency}}. Replace :462's rewrite-wiring sentence with whichever applies.

title: Custom agent Lorebook Writer section (one target lorebook) missing
skill_evidence: absent — references/agents.md:249 'Lorebook-writing agents' covers lorebook_update order / Read Behind / chunked backfill only
reality: With Edit lorebooks on, custom agents get a Lorebook Writer section: Allow lorebook entry writes (settings.lorebookWriteEnabled) lets the agent call the save_lorebook_entry function, but only into the one lorebook picked in Target lorebook (settings.writableLorebookId). The switch stays disabled until Edit lorebooks is on. Create lorebooks lets an agent create a new agent-made lorebook when its lore output has no target, and the lorebook_update result type accepts either edit_lorebooks or create_lorebooks. Sources: docs/agents/custom-agents.md ('If you turn on Edit lorebooks, a Lorebook Writer section appears…'), AgentEditor.tsx:2524-2570, en.json ui.agents.agenteditor.lorebookWriter / allowLorebookEntryWrites / targetLorebook / letsThisCustomAgentCallAFunctionThatCreates, AgentEditor.tsx:427 requiredAnyCapability ['edit_lorebooks','create_lorebooks'], types/agent.ts:742.
fix: Under 'Lorebook-writing agents' add: 'Two routes: the lorebook_update result type (needs Edit lorebooks or Create lorebooks), or the Lorebook Writer section (Edit lorebooks → Allow lorebook entry writes + Target lorebook), which lets the agent call save_lorebook_entry against exactly one chosen book. Create lorebooks lets it create a new book when output has no target.'

title: Review Agent Outputs approval semantics not explained
skill_evidence: references/agents.md:485 lists 'Review Agent Outputs' as a Chat Settings → Agents control with no behavior; :136 card-evolution 'proposes character-card edits for user approval'
reality: With Review Agent Outputs on, lorebook updates, summary updates and other reviewable writer-agent outputs wait in a Review Lorebook Update / Review Summary Update window (Accept / Regenerate / Discard, editable Proposed Text, queue count). With it off, lorebook and summary writes save automatically. Character-card edits and creations always go through Review Character Card Updates (Approve / Regenerate / Reject, stale-edit Override stale) whatever the switch says. Sources: docs/agents/approvals-and-agent-suite.md; docs/agents/agents-overview.md; docs/agents/memory.md ('If your chat requires agent write approval… AI-generated summaries wait'); code: ChatSettingsDrawer.tsx:7734-7745 (descriptions lorebookSummaryCharacterCardUpdatesAndReviewableWriterAgent / lorebookAndSummaryUpdatesCanBeCommittedAutomaticallyCharacter).
fix: Add a short 'Approvals' paragraph near Agent Suite (or under Lorebook-writing agents): 'Review Agent Outputs (Chat Settings → Agents, per chat) holds lorebook and summary writes for Accept / Regenerate / Discard; off = they save automatically. Card edits (Card Evolution Auditor, update_about_me public edits) and character_card_create proposals always need approval.' Point to docs/agents/approvals-and-agent-suite.md.

title: World Maps: shared worlds, templates and travel model not covered
skill_evidence: references/agents.md:150 covers install, 5,000-location cap, navigation and 2.3.3 fixes only
reality: docs/agents/hierarchical-maps.md (World Maps 1.3.1): an account-wide world library of Independent templates (Use template / Add to chat make independent copies) and Shared worlds (Link to chat / Use shared world). A linked chat keeps its own location and history, and its edits stay an unpublished draft until Publish / Discard / Detach and keep copy. Locations have a public description, AI-only private model memory and exact-location lore; only the current location's details reach the prompt (parents give just their names); limits are 5,000 locations and 20 hierarchy levels. Travel: Set destination / Plan route queues one hierarchical step, committed with the next user message. Only the latest user message can authorize movement or discovery; AI narration alone never moves the map. Regenerate and continue don't consume queued moves. Set current story location corrects saved state. Import and export use .hierarchical-map.json. Changelog (2.4.x, #4618) added step-by-step vs immediate travel modes.
fix: Add 3-5 lines after agents.md:150: library (templates vs shared worlds, Publish/Detach), what reaches the model (current location only, private model memory, exact-location lore), the travel rule (queued destination/route commits with the next user turn; user message authorizes moves, narration never does; Set current story location to correct), limits (5,000 locations / 20 levels), and a pointer to docs/agents/hierarchical-maps.md.

title: Memory Recall 'needs an embedding source' omits built-in fallback and default-on
skill_evidence: references/agents.md:353 'Memory Recall | Built-in embedding retrieval over past messages (Chat Settings → Memory Recall → Enable Memory Recall). Needs an embedding source configured; re-vectorize after changing embedding models.'
reality: With no embedding connection set, Memory Recall falls back to a built-in local embedding model that downloads once and runs locally (docs/agents/memory.md 'The embedding source'; code memory-recall-embedding.ts:323 `resolveMemoryRecallEmbeddingSource(...) !== null || isLocalEmbedderAvailable()`). Enable Memory Recall is on by default in Conversation chats and in Roleplay/Game chats with an active Scene. Chunks are stored in the background whenever an embedding source exists, even with the toggle off; the toggle only controls injection. Marinara Lite builds hide the feature. Tools: Memories for This Chat (export/import/rebuild/clear).
fix: agents.md:353 → 'Uses the connection's Semantic Search (Embeddings) source, else the built-in local embedder (one-time download). On by default in Conversation and in Roleplay/Game scene chats. Stores chunks even when the toggle is off (the toggle only controls injection); rebuild in Memories for This Chat after changing embedding models.'

title: 'No .env change needed' contradicts custom-repo ENABLE_CUSTOM_AGENT_REPOS requirement
skill_evidence: references/agents.md:345 'External imports (files, folders, custom repositories) are locked until Settings → Advanced → Danger Zone → Allow custom Agent imports is on — no `.env` change needed.' vs :72 'set `ENABLE_CUSTOM_AGENT_REPOS=true` on the server, enable … Allow custom Agent imports'
reality: The Danger Zone switch itself needs no environment variable, but custom repositories also need ENABLE_CUSTOM_AGENT_REPOS=true (docs/CONFIGURATION.md 'Custom agent repositories'; .env.example:214 default false; runtime-config.ts:713). Files and folders need only the switch.
fix: agents.md:345 → 'Imported agent files and folders are locked until … Allow custom Agent imports is on (no .env change). Custom repositories need that switch plus ENABLE_CUSTOM_AGENT_REPOS=true (see Custom GitHub agent repositories above).'

title: Regenerate reuses cached pre-generation injections; Knowledge agents don't re-run
skill_evidence: references/agents.md:109-110 (knowledge-retrieval / knowledge-router) and :306 Cached prompt injections — no statement that regeneration reuses them
reality: docs/agents/knowledge-sources.md: 'these agents do not run again when you regenerate an existing reply. They run only on new turns.' Code generate.routes.ts:6662-6677 reuses cached context injections on regenerate (Director nudges and Secret Plot excepted), including Knowledge Retrieval/Router output. The Cached prompt injections panel can't re-run the Knowledge agents (approvals-and-agent-suite.md). Knowledge Router can also shortlist candidates by meaning when the lorebook is vectorized and falls back to keywords otherwise (knowledge-sources.md 'Optional semantic shortlisting'; knowledge-router.ts semanticShortlistLorebookEntries).
fix: agents.md:306: add 'Regenerating a reply reuses its cached pre-generation injections (except Narrative Director nudges), so Knowledge Retrieval/Router and context-injection agents don't re-run until a new turn.' Optionally add to :110: 'can shortlist semantically when the lorebook is vectorized.'

title: Uninstall deletes the package's agent configuration and chat selections
skill_evidence: absent — references/agents.md:58/:74-79 package lifecycle; per-package notes say vaults/data survive (:131, :151, :159)
reality: Uninstalling removes the package's agents from every chat's active selection and per-chat agent settings, and deletes their agent configs, including user prompt-template overrides. Chat messages and history are kept. Sources: capability-packages.routes.ts:290-304 (buildCapabilityAgentCleanupPatch + agents.remove); docs/agents/agents-overview.md 'Uninstalling a catalog package removes its code and settings from the Engine while preserving chat messages and history'; optional-agent-packages.md 'Uninstallation'.
fix: Add to Package lifecycle: 'Uninstall removes the package from chats and deletes its agent settings and prompt overrides (history stays; some packages keep their data — see each entry). Use Copy agent first to keep a customized prompt as a custom agent.'
